subject: Demo access issue — calendar invite shows unknown organizer / alternate join link
messages:
From: Elaine Chow <elaine.chow@acerotech.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Mar 2025 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Demo tomorrow — join link failing in calendar invite

Hi Soojin / Ben,

We were just checking the calendar invite for tomorrow’s demo (11:00am PT) and the guest join button is greyed out. When I open the event details it shows the organizer as "Unknown user" and the Meet link returns a 403. I tried from both my Google account and a vendor account and get the same result.

Can you send an alternate join link or reshare the invite? We have two additional folks (Sam Gold, Engineering; Priya Mehta, Security) who need to join.

Attached a quick screenshot of the invite UI and error.

Thanks,
Elaine
Elaine Chow | Senior Product Manager, AceroTech
attachments: screenshot-invite-error.png

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Chow <elaine.chow@acerotech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Mar 2025 15:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Demo tomorrow — join link failing in calendar invite

Thanks for the heads-up, Elaine — sorry for the friction.

Two quick notes:
- We see periodic organizer-token rotation issues when invites are forwarded or when the organizer is an alias; that can strip the Meet metadata which results in the behaviour you saw.
- I’ll ask Ben to provision a temporary Zoom meeting (host bond to our demo host) and resend a clean ICS. That will get you into the session immediately and preserve the scheduled time.

Ben — can you spin up a one-off Zoom link and attach an ICS (alt-ics-snapshot.eml) to this thread? Also please add Sam and Priya to the CAL attendee list so they get a proper invite. If you hit host-token errors when claiming the meeting, use the fallback host email ben+demo@redwood.com (I’ll watch host transfer).

Elaine — once you confirm you can join from the Zoom link I’ll mark this as the canonical join method for tomorrow and include brief host takeover instructions in the invite body.

Sooj
Soojin Lee | Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Elaine Chow <elaine.chow@acerotech.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Mar 2025 16:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Demo tomorrow — join link failing in calendar invite

On it — created temporary Zoom and regenerated an ICS.

Zoom: https://zoom.us/j/9876543210?pwd=ephemeral-token
Passcode: demo2025
Attached: alt-ics-snapshot.eml / temp-zoom-link.txt

Action items I took:
- Created one-off Zoom meeting and set demo host to ben+demo@redwood.com; configured co-host privileges for soojin_lee.
- Resent a fresh calendar invite (Elaine, you should see the updated event in your calendar now). If it still shows unknown organizer, accept the invite and then open the event details — the Zoom join button is reliable even if Meet metadata is missing.

If Sam / Priya still can’t access, we can add them as optional attendees from the event UI and I’ll push them a direct calendaring email.

Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: alt-ics-snapshot.eml; temp-zoom-link.txt

From: Elaine Chow <elaine.chow@acerotech.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Mar 2025 18:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Demo tomorrow — join link failing in calendar invite

Thanks Ben — I see the Zoom link and got the updated invite. Confirmed access from my corporate account (accepted). Sam Gold (sam.gold@acerotech.com) is in and I just added Priya Mehta (priya.mehta@acerotech.com) — she had an SSO block earlier but accepted after I forwarded the new invite.

One ask: can you keep the original meeting time (11:00am PT) and not change the organizer name in the subject? Our execs reference the original title in their calendars.

Also, could you paste a one-paragraph note in the invite body about how to claim host if the current host token expires? We occasionally have token rotation during scheduled events and that helps our security team.

Elaine

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Chow <elaine.chow@acerotech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Mar 2025 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Demo tomorrow — join link failing in calendar invite

Great — glad that worked and thanks for the quick confirmation.

I kept the original subject/title unchanged and attached a short snippet in the invite body: 
"If the meeting host token expires during the session: 1) Request host transfer to ben+demo@redwood.com via the Zoom UI; 2) Ben (or Soojin) will accept transfer and re-grant co-host to the Redwood presenter; 3) If host transfer is blocked by your SSO policy, dial the backup join number in the invite and Ben will start the cloud recording and admit attendees manually."

I’ve also uploaded the runbook we use for these handoffs to the shared drive: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/AceroTech/demo-runbook.pdf

See you all tomorrow at 11:00am PT.

Sooj
